meta.title: Isyarat — Portfolio
meta.description: An Indonesian Sign Language (BISINDO) translator that runs entirely in the browser: signs become text and speech, and no video ever leaves the device.

home.lede: BISINDO signs become text and speech, right in your browser. Your video never leaves the device.
home.manifesto: Sign language is a complete language, with its own grammar, feeling and accents. This project does not replace sign language interpreters. It is a small bridge for everyday conversation, made with respect for the Deaf community.

translate.title: Signs become writing.
translate.intro: Turn on your camera, then fingerspell in BISINDO letters — or switch to Words for 63 basic word signs. Everything is processed on your device.

tips: Light from the front, not behind you.
A plain background helps but is not required.
Your whole hand in view, about half an arm from the camera.

bisindo.title: A language born from its community.
bisindo.lede: BISINDO, Indonesian Sign Language, grew naturally within the Deaf community. It has its own grammar, expressions and regional accents — it is not Indonesian translated onto the hands.

sections.label: Language
sections.title: More than hand movements
sections.body: In BISINDO, meaning is carried by handshape, location, movement and facial expression all at once. Raised eyebrows can turn a statement into a question. That is why automatic translators — including the one on this site — capture only a small part of the full language.

sections.label: Accents
sections.title: One language, many accents
sections.body: Like spoken languages, BISINDO varies by region. The sign for a word in Jakarta can differ from Yogyakarta or Makassar. This model was trained on a small number of signers, so other accents may not be recognised well yet.

sections.label: Identity
sections.title: Deaf, with a capital D
sections.body: Many in the community choose the word Tuli (Deaf) — capitalised — as a cultural and linguistic identity rather than a medical label. This site follows that choice.

bisindo.compareIntro: Two signing systems are used in Indonesia, and they are often confused.
compareRows: Grew naturally in the Deaf community
Everyday conversation in the Deaf community
etiquette: Face the person, keep your mouth uncovered, and speak naturally.
Write or type when needed — it is perfectly fine and often fastest.
Learn a few basic signs: hello, thank you, sorry, name.
For anything important (health, legal, work), use a professional sign language interpreter — not an app.
Ask how the person prefers to communicate.
bisindo.learnBody: The best way to learn BISINDO is from Deaf signers themselves. Look for classes run by local communities, such as those organised by Pusbisindo (Indonesian Sign Language Centre) or Gerkatin chapters in your area.
bisindo.attributionIntro: The models on this site were trained on the public datasets below. Thank you to their authors and to the signers who recorded them.
bisindo.attributionNote: This site is non-commercial. Data without a written licence is used in good faith with full attribution; if an owner objects, it will be removed and the models retrained.

lab.title: How it works.
lab.lede: The case study behind this translator: from light entering the camera to a letter or word on the screen — all on your device.

pipeline.title: Camera
pipeline.body: Video is read directly in the browser. Not a single frame is sent or stored.

pipeline.title: Hand points
pipeline.body: MediaPipe finds 21 points on each hand — both hands at once, since many BISINDO signs use two.

pipeline.title: Features
pipeline.body: The points become 131 numbers: positions relative to the wrist, scaled by palm size. Independent of skin tone, background or distance to the camera.

pipeline.title: Model
pipeline.body: A small neural network (ONNX) guesses the letter from those numbers in under a millisecond.

pipeline.title: Stabiliser
pipeline.body: Guesses are smoothed across frames; a letter is committed after being held for about half a second, so subtitles don't flicker.

pipeline.title: Text & speech
pipeline.body: Letters become words, which can be read aloud, copied or downloaded.

lab.resultsIntro: The model is tested strictly: each time, one whole dataset is held out — people, cameras and rooms never seen in training — and the model guesses the letters in it.
lab.perLetterNote: Computed over all test examples, most of which come from the landmark dataset. Letters with similar shapes, or that involve movement, are confused most often.
lab.wordsPending: Word model results are not available yet.
limits: The word vocabulary is limited to 63 basic signs; full sentences are not translated yet.
Moving signs, facial expression and BISINDO grammar are not captured yet.
Dim light, hands cut off by the frame, or extreme angles reduce accuracy.
Training data comes from few signers; other regional accents may be recognised less well.
It is an everyday aid — not a replacement for a sign language interpreter.
lab.privacy: All camera processing happens in your browser. Models and libraries are downloaded once from this site, then work without a server. No analytics, tracking cookies or recordings.
lab.wordsIntro: The word model is tested per signer: each fold holds out one signer from every dataset, so words are always guessed from people the model has never seen.
lab.wordsMeanLabel: mean word accuracy on new signers
lab.wordsTop3Label: right answer within the top 3 guesses
lab.perWordNote: Words with similar movement — such as greetings that differ only at the end — are confused most often.
